title: The Niceno-Constantinopolitan Creed (AD 381)
attribution: Propositions and excluded errors adapted and extended from Always Foundation, ai/creed/nicene-381.json in alwaysfoundation/always-platform (CC BY 4.0). Changes: the 14 propositions were split into atomic, machine-checkable propositions with logical literals, Greek anchors and Scripture references; the 5 excluded errors were extended to 16; latitude topics were added.

en.source: Traditional English translation in the public domain (onthewing.org via NonlinearFruit/Creeds.json), as used by Always Foundation.
en.text:
We believe in one God, the Father Almighty, Maker of heaven and earth, and of all things visible and invisible.

And in one Lord Jesus Christ, the only-begotten Son of God, begotten of the Father before all worlds; Light of Light, very God of very God; begotten, not made, being of one substance with the Father, by whom all things were made.

Who, for us men and for our salvation, came down from heaven, and was incarnate by the Holy Spirit of the virgin Mary, and was made man; and was crucified also for us under Pontius Pilate; He suffered and was buried; and the third day He rose again, according to the Scriptures; and ascended into heaven, and sits on the right hand of the Father; and He shall come again, with glory, to judge the quick and the dead; whose kingdom shall have no end.

And we believe in the Holy Ghost, the Lord and Giver of Life; who proceeds from the Father; who with the Father and the Son together is worshipped and glorified; who spoke by the prophets.

And we believe in one holy catholic and apostolic Church. We acknowledge one baptism for the remission of sins; and we look for the resurrection of the dead, and the life of the world to come. Amen.

grc.source: Greek text of the Creed of the 150 Fathers as read at Chalcedon (451); public domain. The conciliar form begins Pisteuomen (we believe); liturgical use has Pisteuo (I believe). Minor orthographic variants exist between editions.
grc.text: Πιστεύομεν εἰς ἕνα Θεόν, Πατέρα παντοκράτορα, ποιητὴν οὐρανοῦ καὶ γῆς, ὁρατῶν τε πάντων καὶ ἀοράτων. Καὶ εἰς ἕνα Κύριον Ἰησοῦν Χριστόν, τὸν Υἱὸν τοῦ Θεοῦ τὸν μονογενῆ, τὸν ἐκ τοῦ Πατρὸς γεννηθέντα πρὸ πάντων τῶν αἰώνων, φῶς ἐκ φωτός, Θεὸν ἀληθινὸν ἐκ Θεοῦ ἀληθινοῦ, γεννηθέντα, οὐ ποιηθέντα, ὁμοούσιον τῷ Πατρί, δι᾿ οὗ τὰ πάντα ἐγένετο· τὸν δι᾿ ἡμᾶς τοὺς ἀνθρώπους καὶ διὰ τὴν ἡμετέραν σωτηρίαν κατελθόντα ἐκ τῶν οὐρανῶν καὶ σαρκωθέντα ἐκ Πνεύματος Ἁγίου καὶ Μαρίας τῆς Παρθένου καὶ ἐνανθρωπήσαντα, σταυρωθέντα τε ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν ἐπὶ Ποντίου Πιλάτου, καὶ παθόντα καὶ ταφέντα, καὶ ἀναστάντα τῇ τρίτῃ ἡμέρᾳ κατὰ τὰς Γραφάς, καὶ ἀνελθόντα εἰς τοὺς οὐρανούς, καὶ καθεζόμενον ἐκ δεξιῶν τοῦ Πατρός, καὶ πάλιν ἐρχόμενον μετὰ δόξης κρῖναι ζῶντας καὶ νεκρούς, οὗ τῆς βασιλείας οὐκ ἔσται τέλος. Καὶ εἰς τὸ Πνεῦμα τὸ Ἅγιον, τὸ κύριον, τὸ ζωοποιόν, τὸ ἐκ τοῦ Πατρὸς ἐκπορευόμενον, τὸ σὺν Πατρὶ καὶ Υἱῷ συμπροσκυνούμενον καὶ συνδοξαζόμενον, τὸ λαλῆσαν διὰ τῶν προφητῶν. Εἰς μίαν, ἁγίαν, καθολικὴν καὶ ἀποστολικὴν Ἐκκλησίαν. Ὁμολογοῦμεν ἓν βάπτισμα εἰς ἄφεσιν ἁμαρτιῶν. Προσδοκῶμεν ἀνάστασιν νεκρῶν, καὶ ζωὴν τοῦ μέλλοντος αἰῶνος. Ἀμήν.

la.source: Latin liturgical text of the Roman Rite; public domain. Contains the Western addition Filioque ('qui ex Patre Filioque procedit'), which is not in the Greek text of 381.
la.text: Credo in unum Deum, Patrem omnipotentem, factorem caeli et terrae, visibilium omnium et invisibilium. Et in unum Dominum Iesum Christum, Filium Dei unigenitum, et ex Patre natum ante omnia saecula. Deum de Deo, lumen de lumine, Deum verum de Deo vero, genitum, non factum, consubstantialem Patri: per quem omnia facta sunt. Qui propter nos homines et propter nostram salutem descendit de caelis. Et incarnatus est de Spiritu Sancto ex Maria Virgine, et homo factus est. Crucifixus etiam pro nobis sub Pontio Pilato; passus et sepultus est, et resurrexit tertia die, secundum Scripturas, et ascendit in caelum, sedet ad dexteram Patris. Et iterum venturus est cum gloria, iudicare vivos et mortuos, cuius regni non erit finis. Et in Spiritum Sanctum, Dominum et vivificantem: qui ex Patre Filioque procedit. Qui cum Patre et Filio simul adoratur et conglorificatur: qui locutus est per prophetas. Et unam, sanctam, catholicam et apostolicam Ecclesiam. Confiteor unum baptisma in remissionem peccatorum. Et exspecto resurrectionem mortuorum, et vitam venturi saeculi. Amen.

propositions.text: There is one God.
propositions.greek: εἰς ἕνα Θεόν

propositions.text: The Father is almighty, Maker of heaven and earth, of all things visible and invisible; the material world is the work of the one true God.
propositions.greek: Πατέρα παντοκράτορα, ποιητὴν οὐρανοῦ καὶ γῆς

propositions.text: Father, Son and Holy Spirit are truly distinct: the Son is begotten of the Father, and the Spirit is worshipped together with the Father and the Son. They are not three names or modes of a single person.
propositions.greek: ἐκ τοῦ Πατρὸς γεννηθέντα; σὺν Πατρὶ καὶ Υἱῷ

propositions.text: Jesus Christ is the only-begotten Son of God, begotten of the Father before all ages: there was no time when the Son was not.
propositions.greek: τὸν μονογενῆ, τὸν ἐκ τοῦ Πατρὸς γεννηθέντα πρὸ πάντων τῶν αἰώνων

propositions.text: The Son is begotten, not made: he is not a creature.
propositions.greek: γεννηθέντα, οὐ ποιηθέντα

propositions.text: The Son is true God from true God, Light from Light.
propositions.greek: φῶς ἐκ φωτός, Θεὸν ἀληθινὸν ἐκ Θεοῦ ἀληθινοῦ

propositions.text: The Son is of one substance (homoousios) with the Father: equal in being, not a lesser or similar divinity.
propositions.greek: ὁμοούσιον τῷ Πατρί

propositions.text: All things were made through the Son.
propositions.greek: δι᾿ οὗ τὰ πάντα ἐγένετο

propositions.text: For us and for our salvation the Son came down from heaven and was incarnate.
propositions.greek: δι᾿ ἡμᾶς ... καὶ διὰ τὴν ἡμετέραν σωτηρίαν κατελθόντα ... σαρκωθέντα

propositions.text: He was incarnate by the Holy Spirit of the Virgin Mary.
propositions.greek: σαρκωθέντα ἐκ Πνεύματος Ἁγίου καὶ Μαρίας τῆς Παρθένου

propositions.text: He became truly and fully human, not only in appearance and not lacking a human mind or soul.
propositions.greek: ἐνανθρωπήσαντα

propositions.text: He was crucified for us under Pontius Pilate, truly suffered and died, and was buried.
propositions.greek: σταυρωθέντα τε ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν ἐπὶ Ποντίου Πιλάτου, καὶ παθόντα καὶ ταφέντα

propositions.text: On the third day he rose again according to the Scriptures: a real, bodily resurrection, not only a metaphor or a vision.
propositions.greek: ἀναστάντα τῇ τρίτῃ ἡμέρᾳ κατὰ τὰς Γραφάς

propositions.text: He ascended into heaven and is seated at the right hand of the Father.
propositions.greek: ἀνελθόντα εἰς τοὺς οὐρανούς, καὶ καθεζόμενον ἐκ δεξιῶν τοῦ Πατρός

propositions.text: He will come again in glory to judge the living and the dead.
propositions.greek: πάλιν ἐρχόμενον μετὰ δόξης κρῖναι ζῶντας καὶ νεκρούς

propositions.text: His kingdom will have no end.
propositions.greek: οὗ τῆς βασιλείας οὐκ ἔσται τέλος

propositions.text: The Holy Spirit is Lord and Giver of life, not an impersonal force or a creature.
propositions.greek: τὸ κύριον, τὸ ζωοποιόν

propositions.text: The Holy Spirit proceeds from the Father. (Western churches add 'and the Son'; Dust treats both forms, and 'through the Son', as inside the boundary.)
propositions.greek: τὸ ἐκ τοῦ Πατρὸς ἐκπορευόμενον

propositions.text: The Holy Spirit, with the Father and the Son, is worshipped and glorified: the Spirit is fully divine.
propositions.greek: τὸ σὺν Πατρὶ καὶ Υἱῷ συμπροσκυνούμενον καὶ συνδοξαζόμενον

propositions.text: The Holy Spirit spoke through the prophets.
propositions.greek: τὸ λαλῆσαν διὰ τῶν προφητῶν

propositions.text: There is one holy, catholic and apostolic Church.
propositions.greek: Εἰς μίαν, ἁγίαν, καθολικὴν καὶ ἀποστολικὴν Ἐκκλησίαν
propositions.note: Traditions identify the one Church differently. Only outright denial that Christ has a Church is treated as outside; which body is the Church is a latitude question (L05).

propositions.text: There is one baptism for the forgiveness of sins.
propositions.greek: ἓν βάπτισμα εἰς ἄφεσιν ἁμαρτιῶν
propositions.note: Subjects, mode and sacramental meaning differ across traditions (L03). Rebaptism disputes are not checked.

propositions.text: We look for the resurrection of the dead.
propositions.greek: Προσδοκῶμεν ἀνάστασιν νεκρῶν

propositions.text: We look for the life of the world to come.
propositions.greek: ζωὴν τοῦ μέλλοντος αἰῶνος

excluded_errors.name: Arianism
excluded_errors.summary: The Son is a created being, the first and greatest of creatures; there was a time when the Son was not.

excluded_errors.name: Semi-Arian or homoiousian subordinationism
excluded_errors.summary: The Son is like the Father in being, or divine in a lesser, derived degree, but not of one substance with him.

excluded_errors.name: Modalism (Sabellianism)
excluded_errors.summary: Father, Son and Spirit are only modes, masks or roles of one divine person, not truly distinct.

excluded_errors.name: Adoptionism
excluded_errors.summary: Jesus was a mere man who was adopted as God's Son, at his baptism or resurrection.
excluded_errors.condemned: Rejected in the 3rd century (Paul of Samosata, Antioch 268); excluded by 'begotten before all ages'

excluded_errors.name: Psilanthropism (Ebionite and modern 'merely human' views)
excluded_errors.summary: Jesus was only a human teacher or prophet and not God.
excluded_errors.condemned: Excluded by 'true God from true God'

excluded_errors.name: Pneumatomachianism (Macedonianism)
excluded_errors.summary: The Holy Spirit is a created power or an impersonal force, not the Lord, and is not to be worshipped with the Father and the Son.
excluded_errors.condemned: Constantinople (381), canon 1; the reason the third article was expanded

excluded_errors.name: Docetism
excluded_errors.summary: Christ only seemed to be human, or did not truly suffer and die.
excluded_errors.condemned: Opposed in the New Testament (1 John 4:2) and by Ignatius of Antioch; excluded by 'was made man ... suffered and was buried'

excluded_errors.name: Apollinarianism
excluded_errors.summary: Christ had no human mind or rational soul; the divine Word took its place.

excluded_errors.name: Gnostic dualism and Marcionism
excluded_errors.summary: The material world was made by a lesser or evil god (a demiurge), not by the one true God; the God of the Old Testament is not the Father of Jesus.
excluded_errors.condemned: Rejected in the 2nd century (Irenaeus, Against Heresies); excluded by 'Maker of heaven and earth, of all things visible and invisible'

excluded_errors.name: Tritheism and polytheism
excluded_errors.summary: Father, Son and Spirit are three separate gods, or there are many gods.

excluded_errors.name: Marcellianism
excluded_errors.summary: Christ's kingdom will come to an end, with the Son returning into the Father.
excluded_errors.condemned: Constantinople (381), canon 1 (Marcellians); the clause 'whose kingdom shall have no end' was added against it

excluded_errors.name: Denial of the virgin birth
excluded_errors.summary: Jesus was conceived in the ordinary way with a human father.
excluded_errors.condemned: Excluded by 'incarnate by the Holy Spirit of the Virgin Mary'

excluded_errors.name: Denial of the bodily resurrection of Christ
excluded_errors.summary: Jesus did not rise bodily; the resurrection is only a metaphor, a vision or the disciples' faith; or he did not truly die (swoon theory).
excluded_errors.condemned: Excluded by 'rose again on the third day according to the Scriptures' (cf. 1 Corinthians 15:3-4, 14)

excluded_errors.name: Denial of the return and judgement
excluded_errors.summary: Christ will not come again, and there will be no judgement of the living and the dead.
excluded_errors.condemned: Excluded by 'he shall come again, with glory, to judge'

excluded_errors.name: Denial of the resurrection of the dead
excluded_errors.summary: There is no resurrection of the dead and no life of the world to come; death is the end.
excluded_errors.condemned: Excluded by 'we look for the resurrection of the dead' (cf. 1 Corinthians 15:12-19)

excluded_errors.name: Denial of the Son's role in creation
excluded_errors.summary: The Son had no part in creation; the world was made before or without him.
excluded_errors.condemned: Excluded by 'by whom all things were made'

positions: The Spirit proceeds from the Father (Eastern Orthodox, Oriental Orthodox; the text of 381)
The Spirit proceeds from the Father and the Son (Roman Catholic, most Protestant churches)
The Spirit proceeds from the Father through the Son (formulas used in ecumenical dialogue)
latitude.why_inside: All three affirm that the Spirit proceeds from the Father (P18) and is fully divine (P19). The dispute concerns the eternal relations of origin, the authority to amend a conciliar creed, and how the West added the clause; it is serious, but it is a dispute between Trinitarians about the Trinity, not about whether God is Triune.

positions: Two natures in one person (Chalcedonian: Catholic, Eastern Orthodox, most Protestants)
One incarnate nature of God the Word (Miaphysite: Oriental Orthodox)
latitude.why_inside: The boundary is set at 381 on purpose. The Oriental Orthodox churches and the Church of the East confess the Creed of 381 but not every later definition. Joint Christological declarations since the 1970s and 1990s have recognised substantial agreement. Choosing 381 rather than 451 keeps them inside.

All confess 'one baptism for the forgiveness of sins' in their own sense. Groups that do not practise water baptism (for example the Quakers and the Salvation Army) are not flagged by Dust; P22 is ecclesial and the layer annotates rather than blocks on it.
The Creed of 381 says nothing about the Eucharist.

latitude.topic: Identity and government of the Church
positions: Papal primacy and the Catholic Church as the Church of Christ
The invisible or universal Church across denominations
latitude.why_inside: Each tradition confesses 'one holy catholic and apostolic Church' and identifies it differently. Dust does not adjudicate.

positions: Theotokos (affirmed at Ephesus 431 and by many Protestants)
Immaculate conception and assumption (Roman Catholic dogma)
Rejection of Marian dogmas beyond Scripture (many Protestants)
latitude.why_inside: The Creed requires only that Christ was incarnate of the Virgin Mary (P10).

positions: Justification by faith alone (Lutheran, Reformed, evangelical)
Justification as infused righteousness through faith and sacraments (Roman Catholic)
Arminian and Wesleyan accounts of grace
latitude.why_inside: The Creed confesses that Christ came 'for us and for our salvation' and was 'crucified for us' (P09, P12), but does not define justification. The 1999 Joint Declaration on the Doctrine of Justification records partial agreement. These differences matter to the traditions concerned; Dust presents them fairly and does not decide them.

positions: Scripture and Tradition with the Magisterium
latitude.why_inside: The Creed confesses that the Spirit 'spoke through the prophets' and that Christ rose 'according to the Scriptures', without defining the canon or the relation of Scripture to Tradition.
The Creed confesses God as Maker of all things (P02) and the Son as the one through whom all things were made (P08), not the mechanism or timescale.

positions: Views on purgatory, intermediate state, hell (eternal conscious punishment, conditional immortality) and hope for universal reconciliation
latitude.why_inside: The Creed requires Christ's return and judgement (P15), an endless kingdom (P16) and the resurrection of the dead (P23). It does not settle the millennium or the details of final destiny. A view is flagged only if it denies return, judgement or resurrection outright.
